market_summary: Fresh start — P&L and AI-cost tracking reset to zero. The next scheduled run begins the new record.
memo:
History reset on 2026-08-28. Positions below are real and still held; only the measurement baseline was cleared. The equity curve, executed-trades log and position theses start filling from the next run.

Previous history is archived in docs/data/archive/.

signals.note: iPhone/services growth remains modest single-to-low-double-digit while shares sit near record highs on a ~30x forward multiple that already assumes a stronger AI-driven upgrade cycle than guidance supports.
Mid-30s% Azure/AI growth roughly justifies the ~32x forward multiple, though rising capex intensity caps further re-rating upside.
Data-center revenue keeps beating and raising, but the stock's elevated forward multiple has already priced in continued triple-digit growth, leaving little residual edge.
Double-digit Search/Cloud growth with improving margins trades at a discount multiple versus mega-cap peers, a gap that looks wider than the antitrust/AI-disruption risk warrants.
AWS reacceleration and retail margin expansion are running roughly in line with the premium multiple investors are already paying.
Strong ad revenue growth is offset by aggressive AI capex spending, keeping the current multiple reasonably balanced against near-term earnings power.
Delivery growth has stalled while the stock trades at a triple-digit earnings multiple built on unproven robotaxi/humanoid bets rather than current auto fundamentals.
Record trading and net-interest income are already reflected in a premium-to-book valuation versus regional and global bank peers.
Steady double-digit payment-volume growth is matched by a consistent high-20s multiple, leaving minimal valuation gap.
After 2025 guidance cuts and a medical-cost-ratio shock crushed the multiple to historic lows, the price appears to overshoot the downside relative to a normalizing earnings base.
Steady pharma/medtech growth is offset by talc litigation overhang, keeping shares roughly in line with healthcare-sector peers.
Earnings track oil and gas prices closely, and the current multiple sits within historical energy-sector norms.
E-commerce and ad-business momentum are real, but shares have re-rated well above their historical multiple, pricing in near-flawless execution.
Consistent comp-sales growth doesn't fully justify a near-50x earnings multiple, among the richest in retail.
Data-center and power-infrastructure-driven equipment demand is a real tailwind, but the stock's cycle-high valuation already reflects it.
